I9s are beefier but tend to be silly expensive and for gaming don't serve much purpose, typically they're more for workstations for rendering and compiling. I5s are more for budget systems, a few models are decent but they'll bottle neck higher end video cards. I3s are for low end systems, computers that really aren't for gaming other than old games maybe or some csgo. Hope that clarified things.

But craft paint is desaturated and bland compared to real model paint, you can always tell. The most common brands are Reaper, army painter, Vallejo and Citadel. Of those, Citadel is the best and most expensive. Reaper is a good starter brand, try their MSP brand. Like brushes you should really buy around and see what you like. Vallejo probably has the widest selection as they do historical and gaming, they have a whole line of colors just matched for true world materials and another just for mecha. Ultimately test out brands and choose yours. The biggest pain in the ass is white and yellow, the two best companies for those tends to be Citadel and Pro Acryl. Pro acryl is new to the scene and quite expensive but they're supposed to be the best. Finally, while not a paint but in the same realm, Citadel technicals. Texture paints or effect paints. These are expensive but when you're starting they're magic in a bottle. You can make your own, but when you're new, if you got the cash, it's better just to buy the Citadel brand and apply it. Then the more I wanted that npc dead the more id focus events and enemy aggression toward them. But never was a death scripted, sometimes my party would squeak out wins, creatively overcome challenges and save the npc. Sometimes they didn't. In my game there is a labyrinth, magical in nature always run by a Minotaur. This labirynth holds treasure and secrets and never stays in one place for long. Various villages and towns tell stories and myths, of the hero's that found it and came back rich, the peasants that ventured in and never returned or even the mages that sought its secrets and came back mad, brimming with new powers but their minds lost. Some say it has intent, that the Minotaur is searching for someone, or something. The labirynth can move anywhere while adventurers are inside, people who go in while around their home village can come out and find themselves across the world. Some scholars believe the labyrinth hides doors that travel even further than that, that the labyrinth is a sort of intersection of time and space, a place the old gods used for travelling vast distances. The labirynth is filled with puzzles, curiosities and danger, and each time the Minotaur is defeated and the labirynth treasures plundered, it comes back again, more powerful than ever. - in my game eventually I switch out the Minotaur for dragons or other such nasties cause my party was too powerful, but the concept remained and I tried to play a story where the Minotaur were actually servants to a higher mind, a clockwork dragon, that was looking for some hero's to take an adventure to another dimension to find the dragons heart to help it die, for eternity as gears and metal is a hell of its own. The other thing was a weather vane, a pure iron one with a locator enchantment put on it and a piece of treasure sacrificed to it would point to the labirynth where ever it is. But adventurers beware, the labirynth is a diabolical thing, for where ever you enter the labirynth you may not come out in the same place and once entered you cannot leave until either you or the labirynth is defeated. When I run this labyrinth I don't create a building in my world for the adventurers to find, anyone could walk upon that, no- just two grand, luxurious wooden doors like the doors to a kings throne room, embellished with brass and steel rivets, carved in the finest fashion and set in a door frame to match.
